subject: Renewal epoch realignment & surge-capacity path
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Renewal epoch realignment & surge-capacity path

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the productive call last week. Per our conversation, I pulled together a focused proposal so Clearwave can co-term the existing subscription, add a surge capacity buffer for Q3 product rollouts, and lock in a multi-year rate that phases in over an agreed ramp schedule.

High-level summary:
- Term: 24 months (co-term to 2028-03-31) with an optional 12-month auto-renew opt-in at a pre-agreed uplift.
- Ramp: Year 1 base + 30% burst buffer available on demand (metered true-up monthly); Year 2 scales to base + 60% with a scheduled mid-year review and optional front-loaded credits.
- Billing: Quarterly invoice with quarterly true-up (preferred) or monthly invoicing if procurement requires.

I attached a draft contract with the proposed proration language and a surge appendix that outlines operational runbook and throttling fallbacks. Can you confirm: (1) procurement timeline, (2) whether quarterly true-up looks acceptable, and (3) if you want SOC2 evidence & the data-retention language tightened?

Attachments: [Attachment: RW-Contract-Clearwave-v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB)], [Attachment: SOW-Clearwave-surge-appendix.xlsx (XLSX, 240 KB)]

If it helps, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk the legal/procurement team through the ramp mechanics and proration examples.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124
From: Emma Reynolds <emma.reynolds@clearwave.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Renewal epoch realignment & surge-capacity path

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the documents. A few quick items from our side:

1) Procurement timeline: we need legal sign-off and a PO in place before June 25 to hit our fiscal commitments. Mark (cc'd on the thread) is our procurement lead and will own the PO cadence.
2) Quarterly true-up is fine, but we need an explicit cap on invoice variability during Year 1 (we'd like a 20% quarter-to-quarter protection band unless we provide notice 14 days prior to the burst).
3) SOC2: please send the latest report and the encryption-at-rest attestation. Also, Mark will want a short matrix showing which data traverses Redwood's hosted environment vs. our VPC options.

On the surge: the planned product rollout in early Q3 will hit our gen-inference heavily for short windows. We like the idea of a burst buffer, but we need clear SLAs and a runbook for sudden throttling/fallbacks so our customer success team can plan.

I reviewed the contract and have a couple of legal points; we should route the redlines through DocuSign (Mark's preference).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — can Marissa loop in any implementation/ops IP we should expect during onboarding?

Thanks,
Emma Reynolds
Head of Platform Engineering\Clearwave Analytics
emma.reynolds@clearwave.com

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Emma's reply (below). Action items I want us to coordinate before we respond to Clearwave:

- Legal/Procurement: we need a clarified protection band for Year 1. Emma asked for 20% quarter-to-quarter cap unless they provide 14-day notice. Do we accept 20% or counter with 25% and front-loaded credits?
- SOC2 & encryption artifacts: Karthik, can you pull the latest SOC2 Type II, encryption attestation, and a 1-page VPC/data flow matrix for the customer?
- SLA & runbook: Marissa, can you draft a 1-page runbook (on-call escalation + throttling behavior + recommended fallback model) we can include as an appendix to the SOW? Include expected time-to-scale (token/sec thresholds) for our surge nodes.

Proposed internal position: accept quarterly true-up; offer 25% protection band with an option to buy down to 20% with a one-time onboarding credit (we can reserve $35k in partner credits against Year 1 invoices). That preserves economics and gives them budget certainty.

I'll prepare a redline summary and send back to Emma with a revised contract that: (a) includes the 25% protection band + optional credit buy-down, (b) links to SOC2 artifacts, and (c) adds the 1-page runbook.

Emma / Mark —

Thanks for the quick clarifications. Attached is an updated package that reflects our internal position and addresses your asks:

What changed (high level):
- Protection band: added a 25% quarter-to-quarter protection cap in Year 1. We also included an optional one-time onboarding credit of $35,000 that can be applied to Year 1 invoices to effectively reduce the cap to ~20% if Clearwave elects that option within 14 days of signing.
- Billing & true-up: quarterly invoicing with monthly metering details included in the SOW appendix.
- SOC2 & encryption: attached SOC2 Type II redacted summary and an encryption-at-rest attestation. Also included is a simple matrix that shows data flows and hosting options (hosted vs VPC).
- Runbook & SLAs: Marissa attached a 1-page runbook that covers throttling thresholds, automatic fallback behavior (region reroute + model-variant fallback), and who to contact for escalations during a surge.

Attachments: [Attachment: RW-Contract-Clearwave-v3.pdf (PDF, 1.3 MB)], [Attachment: SOC2-Redacted-Summary.pdf (PDF, 420 KB)], [Attachment: SOW-Clearwave-surge-appendix.xlsx (XLSX, 260 KB)]

Next steps we recommend:
1) Mark / Clearwave procurement: confirm PO timeline — if you can provide a draft PO by June 10, we can commit to the co-term cutover and reserve the onboarding credit.
2) Legal redlines: we'll accept DocuSign routing. Please send redlines to legal@redwood.ai and cc me.
3) Ops kickoff: Marissa's team is available for a 30-minute runbook walkthrough next Tue or Wed (dates: 26/27 May).
